clue.text: Escort service provider perhaps — bribe with £500

parts.note: to grease someone's palm is to bribe them
a monkey is British slang for five hundred pounds

explanation.surface: A shady escort agency is paid off with a hefty five-hundred-pound bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Escort is a Ford car, not a companion: whoever services it is a mechanic. A MONKEY is British slang for £500.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a mechanic, the sort of person who would service a Ford Escort car.

clue.text: Ran gaol cruelly as alternative to porridge

indicators.note: cruelly suggests the letters of 'Ran gaol' are treated roughly and knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A harsh prison governor serves something other than porridge — with 'porridge' also slang for a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakfast cereal of baked oats and nuts, eaten instead of a bowl of oatmeal.

clue.text: Beg, heading off from downtown area before time

indicators.note: before places the area letter ahead of the time letter
the head, or first letter, of the word for downtown is cut away

parts.note: the town centre is the downtown district

explanation.surface: Someone pleads to set off from the city centre ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off from' removes the C of CENTRE, leaving ENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to plead earnestly with someone for something.

clue.text: Two features of seaside introducing parking for one that likes paddling

indicators.note: introducing means the second seaside feature has the parking letter brought into it

parts.note: sand and a pier are two things found at the seaside
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A seaside resort with beach and pier gets a car park for paddling holidaymakers.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside PIER, after SAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading shorebird that runs along the water's edge feeding, a playful way to describe it.

clue.text: Operatic heroine's career's beginning to take off

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Bohème

indicators.note: beginning means just the opening letter of career's is used

explanation.surface: An opera diva's career begins to soar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like a career launching; here it means to imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to imitate or parody them.

clue.text: Short literary work Fitzgerald produced after a month

indicators.note: after puts the singer's name behind the month

parts.note: Nov is the abbreviation for November
Ella Fitzgerald, the American jazz singer

explanation.surface: F. Scott Fitzgerald turns out a short book after a month's work.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fitzgerald is the singer Ella, not the novelist F. Scott.
explanation.definitionFit: A prose fiction longer than a short story but shorter than a full-length novel.

clue.text: Ban so restricts business expert

indicators.note: restricts means the word for so hems in the business qualification

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so
an MBA, a Master of Business Administration, is a business expert

explanation.surface: A prohibition is imposed so as to limit a business consultant.
explanation.definitionFit: An official prohibition, especially on trade with a particular country.

clue.text: Husband cheating initially trapped by investigator, the old twister

indicators.note: trapped by means the investigator word encloses the husband and the initial letter

parts.note: a checker is someone who investigates or inspects
hubby is informal for husband

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of cheating is taken

explanation.surface: A cheating husband is caught by a private detective, the old rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped by' puts the husband and C after the first letter of the investigator word. 'twister' suggests a crook; it means a dancer of the Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s American singer whose hit The Twist launched the dance craze.

clue.text: One working in the kitchen cooked sports cuisine

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of sports cuisine are mixed up like ingredients

explanation.surface: A chef prepares food for athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'kitchen' is the orchestra's percussion section, not a place for cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestral slang calls the percussion section the kitchen, so a drummer works there.

clue.text: Encourage team with player sent off after try

indicators.note: after puts the reduced team behind the word for try

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case
a football or cricket team has eleven players, so one sent off leaves ten

explanation.surface: A rugby team down to fourteen is spurred on after scoring a try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' is a rugby score in the surface but means hear a case in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone heart, cheering and emboldening them.

clue.text: See a book spy pocketed, not being secure

indicators.note: pocketed means the spy word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
V stands for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: A spy slips a book into his pocket, a sign that something is insecure.
explanation.walkthrough: V is short for vide, the Latin 'see' used in references.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not fixed or fastened in place can be shifted about.

clue.text: Drip in hostelry coming back for lots of drinks

indicators.note: in places the drip word within the reversed hostelry
coming back means the word for hostelry is read backwards

parts.note: a pub is a hostelry
to drip is to ooze

explanation.surface: A drip, a wet bore, returns to the pub for a heavy session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drip' looks like a dull person in the surface; here it is a verb meaning seep. 'coming back' turns the hostelry round to BUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British phrase for a drinking session where a lot of alcohol is consumed.

clue.text: California men in charge concerned with heat

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Californian men in authority worry about the heatwave.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is the usual crossword way to get men.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective relating to heat or calories, as in the old caloric theory of warmth.

clue.text: Still engages a second worker in brewery

indicators.note: engages means the still word takes on the others within it

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'yet more'

explanation.surface: A brewery hires another hand in the stillroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' suggests a distillery; here it means yet.
explanation.definitionFit: The fungus that ferments the wort is the vital worker in any brewery.

clue.text: Strong wine and potatoes from Indian, they provide temporary relief

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
aloo is the word for potato in Indian cookery

explanation.surface: Port and Indian potato dishes offer short-lived comfort to the diner.
explanation.walkthrough: Portaloos are British portable toilets, so 'relief' is the toilet kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Portable toilets hired for events let people relieve themselves temporarily.

clue.text: Like dodgy joint that could give me haircut

indicators.note: that could give says the letters of 'me haircut' may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A shady den where someone might cut my hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy joint' looks like a seedy establishment but is an aching knee or hip.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing a joint afflicted with rheumatism, stiff and painful.

clue.text: Like some carphones made by robots?

definitions.meaning: a phone used without holding it in the hand
products made by machine need no human hands at all

explanation.surface: Car phones assembled on a robotic production line.
explanation.definitionFit: A device used without hands, and a product made with no human hands involved.

clue.text: Some misdemeanour is hard to encourage

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A minor offence is hard to promote — or to excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish an idea or feeling is to foster and encourage it.

clue.text: Something sparkling cook gently keeps hot

indicators.note: keeps means the gentle cooking word holds the letter for hot

parts.note: to simmer is to cook just below boiling
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A sparkling drink is gently heated and kept warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint glimmering light, a sparkle or gleam.

clue.text: American soldier going after my dog

indicators.note: going after puts the soldier behind the exclamation

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A GI follows the narrator's dog around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh breed of short-legged herding dog, famously kept by the late Queen.

clue.text: Song itinerant plays in company

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled letters within the company abbreviation
itinerant means wandering, so the letters of plays move about

explanation.surface: A travelling theatre company performs a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A West Indian style of song, usually topical and improvised.

clue.text: Calamitous sport with oval ball in America takes over

indicators.note: takes means the American abbreviation takes up the cricket letter before it

parts.note: RU is rugby union, played with an oval ball
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
US is the United States

explanation.surface: American football takes over from rugby with disastrous results.
explanation.definitionFit: Causing ruin or disaster, devastating.

clue.text: Guide broadcast of person cooking spicy food

indicators.note: broadcast of means the word is heard on air rather than read

parts.note: someone making a curry could be called a currier

explanation.surface: A TV cooking show featuring a curry chef acts as a guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour courier is a guide who escorts holiday groups.

clue.text: Geordie teacher got up out of bed

indicators.note: got up means the letters climb, reading backwards in this down clue

parts.note: Geordies come from Newcastle in the North East, NE
pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A Newcastle schoolmaster has got up out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' looks like the definition but signals the upward reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has risen is up and out of bed.

clue.text: Large number move aimlessly forward round island

indicators.note: round means the phrase for moving aimlessly onward goes around the island letter

parts.note: to mill about is to move aimlessly
on means forward, as in 'go on'

explanation.surface: A huge crowd wanders forward round an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand thousand, a very large number.

clue.text: Puzzles formulated in games

indicators.note: formulated means the letters of 'in games' are worked up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Puzzles devised for games.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddles or mysteries, things that are hard to understand.

clue.text: Moves softly, softly forward in games

indicators.note: in places the soft and forward letters within the games word

parts.note: ties are matches in a cup competition
P, piano, is the musical direction for softly
to means forward, as in 'to and fro'

explanation.surface: A player creeps quietly forward during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk on the toes so as to make no noise.

clue.text: Half-heartedly cleaning mule station

indicators.note: half-heartedly means one of the two central letters of the cleaning word is lost

parts.note: charring is doing paid cleaning work, as a charwoman
a mule is a cross between a donkey and a horse

explanation.surface: A grudging cleaner tackles a stubborn mule.
explanation.walkthrough: Charing Cross is a London railway terminus. 'Half-heartedly' drops one R of the RR heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A major London railway terminus near Trafalgar Square.
